---
title: "Midterm: Mini Literature Review"
---

Due **Tuesday November 10, 3:10 PM** (before class), as a single PDF on
Canvas. 90 points. Grading is anonymous.

For your midterm, you will write a mini literature review on a plant genetics
topic of your choice. This is your chance to go deep on something that
genuinely interests you: to learn what has been discovered, how we know it,
and what remains unknown.

## Choosing a topic

The topic is yours, but the strongest reviews usually walk through one of
three doors:

- **A problem plant genetics can help solve** (a disease, a stress, a
  nutrition gap, a sustainability challenge)
- **An open question in plant genetics** (something researchers are actively
  trying to figure out)
- **How a genetic technology works** (and what it makes possible)

Focused beats broad: "genetics of drought tolerance in maize roots" will
write a better two pages than "plant biotechnology."

## How the course supports you

The prompt is live from week 1. On **Thu Oct 15** the library session teaches
literature search tools, followed by in-class work time (bring a laptop). The
**Midterm Topic Explorer** — three candidate topics, a mini lit search on
each, self-scores, and your pick — is due **Thu Oct 22, 3:10 PM** on Canvas.
Then you have until **Nov 10** to write.

## Requirements

- 1–2 pages, single-spaced; 12-point font
- At least 5 peer-reviewed sources
- A descriptive, informative title
- Sections: **Introduction** (why the topic matters), **Discoveries** (the
  main portion — historical research and recent breakthroughs and what they
  mean), **Future Directions** (next questions; enabling tools), **References**
- MLA format for in-text citations and works cited
- Extra credit: an original self-made figure (separate page) that synthesizes
  your review, with a legend, referenced in the text
